what: Three ladders run back-to-back on a deliberately idle box: the S6 engine at rungs 1800/2100, the same engine at rungs 2400/2700, and the pre-S6 engine (node signature 20110404) at rungs 1800/2100 as a contention-matched control. 100 games per rung, 60+0.5s, Threads=1, cycle-98 quant at blend 25 on every arm.
anchor: official SF16 avx2 release, sha256 8f60a016dc767e0d648a8665b8ede3e6e4d28c086ad90517ad26f55b9960bd84, /workspace/stockfish16. UCI_LimitStrength=true, UCI_Elo set per rung, Hash 64, Threads 1 -- verified present in every rung's recorded config.
why_a_control: The 2026-08-08 baseline of 1892 was measured while campaign_v6 was training on 160 threads. This ladder ran on an idle box (load average ~5 across 184 cores, every engine on its own core). Without a matched control there is no way to separate S6's contribution from the difference in CPU contention, so the pre-S6 binary was rebuilt from 0250b61 and run under identical conditions.

result_controlled_s6_improvement.note: THIS is the trustworthy comparison: identical rungs, identical idle box, identical model, only the engine differs.
result_controlled_s6_improvement.interpretation: Independently corroborates the 1000-game paired A/B measurement of +56 Elo [+44, +68] for S6: same direction, same rough magnitude, arrived at against an external opponent rather than by self-play. The paired A/B remains the tighter estimate because pairing removes opening and colour variance; this anchor measurement is noisier (CI spans 150 Elo) but independent.

finding_the_anchor_scale_is_rung_depende.severity: affects every absolute Elo number this campaign has ever quoted
finding_the_anchor_scale_is_rung_depende.observation: The SAME S6 binary, same model, same session, same idle box, measured against different rung pairs:
finding_the_anchor_scale_is_rung_depende.diagnosis: Implied ratings climb monotonically with rung strength (1800 -> 1996, 2100 -> 2239, 2400 -> 2365, 2700 -> 2509). If SF16's UCI_Elo were a consistent Elo scale these would agree. They do not, so UCI_LimitStrength's nominal Elo is compressed relative to real playing strength in this range: the gap between the 1800 and 2700 settings is worth far less than 900 Elo of actual strength.
consequences: No absolute 'PieBot Elo' from this ladder is meaningful without naming its rungs.
Today's numbers CANNOT be compared to the 2026-08-08 baseline of 1892, which used rungs 1500/1800. That comparison is not 1892 -> 2146; it is two different scales.
The mission target of '~2700 on the pinned SF16 anchor scale' is ambiguous as written, because the scale depends on the rungs used to measure it.
The existing protocol rule 'place rungs within +/-400 of expected strength' was treated as a precision guideline. It is stronger than that: outside a fixed rung set the scale itself moves.
finding_the_anchor_scale_is_rung_depende.recommendation: Treat the ladder as a RELATIVE instrument. Fix one canonical rung set and only ever compare within it, or -- better, and what this run did -- always measure the new engine against the old one at matched rungs on a matched machine and report the difference. Absolute ratings should carry their rungs in the same breath, e.g. '2146 @ rungs 1800/2100'.

method_note: S6's rung-1800 score rate as games accumulated: 100% (5g) -> 86.1% (18g) -> 80.2% (58g) -> 79.2% (72g) -> 75.5% (100g). A headline taken from the early sample would have overstated the result by more than 20 percentage points. Full samples only.
